name: Refugio antiaéreo de la Plaza Tetuán, Castelló de la Plana
story: Castelló was bombed by Nationalist and Italian aircraft as the front approached in spring 1938, and it fell to Nationalist troops in June 1938 during the drive towards Valencia. This public shelter under Plaza Tetuán was built in 1937–38 to protect the townspeople. Restored and opened as a site of the city museum (MUCC), it presents the war as civilians lived it: the raids, the sirens and the shelter network, and life in a city that changed hands in the middle of the war.
see: A restored underground shelter with exhibits and multimedia; audioguides in Spanish, Valencian, English and French.
plan: Free entry; open Tuesday to Saturday 16:00–19:00 and Sunday 10:00–14:00, closed Mondays and in heavy rain. Guided tour at 19:00 (book on 964 73 52 17). Self-guided visit about 45 minutes, maximum 60 people inside.
